_meta.indication: Treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients who have a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 53 skipping; approved under accelerated approval based on an increase in dystrophin production.

pivotal_trials.phase: First-in-human study conducted in two parts (dose-titration Part 1 and open-label extension Part 2)
pivotal_trials.design: Study 1 Part 1 was a double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-titration study in 12 DMD patients randomized 2:1 to VYONDYS 53 or placebo; Part 2 was a 168-week open-label study at 30 mg/kg/week.
pivotal_trials.population: DMD patients with a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene amenable to exon 53 skipping; median age 8 years, on stable corticosteroids.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary biological endpoint: change from Baseline to Week 48 of Part 2 in dystrophin levels in biceps muscle biopsy determined by western blot.
pivotal_trials.n: 25 patients in Study 1 Part 2 (12 from Part 1 plus 13 additional treatment-naive patients)
pivotal_trials.result: Dystrophin levels increased from 0.10% of normal at baseline to 1.02% of normal after 48 weeks; mean change from baseline was 0.92% (p<0.001); median change 0.88%.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=20% and higher than placebo) were headache (41% vs 10%), pyrexia (41% vs 14%), fall (29% vs 19%), abdominal pain (27% vs 10%), nasopharyngitis (27% vs 14%), cough (27% vs 19%), vomiting (27% vs 19%), and nausea (20% vs 10%). Warnings include hypersensitivity reactions and renal toxicity.
target_moa: Golodirsen is an antisense oligonucleotide of the phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PMO) subclass designed to bind to exon 53 of dystrophin pre-mRNA, causing exon 53 skipping to allow production of an internally truncated dystrophin protein.
modality: oligonucleotide (antisense oligonucleotide, phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer subclass)

rems.type: No safety risks were identified which would require a REMS at this time.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not referred to an advisory committee because the safety profile was acceptable, the trial designs were acceptable, and the surrogate marker findings were clear.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Dystrophin biomarker data (increase in dystrophin production in skeletal muscle) proposed as a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

citations.quote: 3690-1 In order to verify the clinical benefit of golodirsen, complete Study 4045-301, A Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Multicenter Study With an Open-Label Extension to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of SRP-4045 and SRP-4053 in Patients With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy. The study includes a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled period of 96 weeks, and concludes after an open-label extension period to 144 weeks. The primary endpoint will be the 6-minute walk test.

summary.text: Golodirsen received Fast Track designation and Orphan drug designation for DMD, with Priority Review of the NDA. It was approved under the accelerated approval pathway based on dystrophin biomarker data proposed as a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, after an initial Complete Response letter and a granted appeal; continued approval is contingent on verifying clinical benefit in confirmatory Study 4045-301.
